memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So at the Lord's command Moses sent them out from the Desert of Paran. All of them were leaders of the Israelites. These are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur; from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori; from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh; from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph; from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun; from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu; from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi; from the tribe of Manasseh (a tribe of Joseph), Gaddi son of Susi; from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli; from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael; from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi; from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Maki. These are the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. (Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.) — Num 13:3-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A list of twelve names, one leader from each tribe. It is tempting to skim past a passage like this, but God thought these names worth recording. Every man here was a chosen representative, a leader trusted with an important mission on behalf of his whole tribe.

Most of these names we never hear again. Only two — Caleb and Joshua — will stand out in the story that follows. Yet all twelve were given the same opportunity, the same mission, the same evidence. What made the difference between them was not their position or their pedigree, but their faith. Ten would shrink back; two would trust God.

There is a quiet detail tucked at the end: Moses renamed Hoshea as Joshua. The name means "the Lord saves." It is the same name, in its Greek form, as "Jesus." Long before this young man became Israel's great leader into the promised land, he carried a name pointing to the greater Deliverer who would one day lead His people into an eternal inheritance.

God records ordinary names because He values individuals. You may feel like one small name on a long list, unnoticed and unremarkable. But the God who wrote down twelve tribal leaders knows your name too. The question that mattered for them is the same one that matters for us: when God speaks, will we trust Him?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe your name and your faith matter to God, even if you feel unremarkable?
2. What tends to make the difference between those who trust God and those who shrink back?
3. How does it encourage you that "the Lord saves" was written into Joshua's very name?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You know my name and value me as an individual. When You give me a mission, help me to respond with faith like Caleb and Joshua. Thank You for Jesus, in whom the Lord truly saves. Amen.
